To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the proposed segment-based policy is the most efficient policy in terms of update frequency; 2) the update frequency can be significantly reduced by using a map-matching algorithm to identify the road on which a moving object is traveling; 3) the update frequency is further reduced by using a prediction-based update algorithm, which predicts the position of an object at a future time and compares it with the position at a later time to decide if an update is needed.

(a) the segment-based policy is more accurate than a state-of-the-art policy, (b) the segment-based approach is robust to errors in map matching, and (c) the segment-based update policy is efficient, in that it reduces update volume by a factor of 10 compared with the state-of-the-art approach
the proposed segment-based policy for moving objects outperforms the existing policies, both with respect to the number of updates and the prediction error.
